non_negotiable_invariants: Every capability reachable today stays reachable: no control, route, permission semantic, durable state transition, recovery path or error behaviour may be removed or silently altered by a UI change.

Authorization, approval, admission and sandbox semantics are server-authored; the UI renders them and never decides them. A disabled control must reflect an authoritative refusal, not a client-side guess.
No new privilege, no new outbound request, no new dependency or CDN, and no framework migration without measured justification recorded in docs/adr/.
Durable state and API contracts are unchanged unless the story explicitly says otherwise and a backend test proves the transition.
Untrusted text from models, repositories or tools never grants authority and never becomes markup that can execute.
Evidence over claims: screenshots, keyboard walks and test output are recorded as they happened; skipped or environment-blocked checks are reported as skipped.
One story per branch and pull request; the shared ledger is the only claim mechanism.

decisions: A URL segment chosen at runtime is a dynamic match with candidates, never an exact match: guessing one of two routes would turn a finding into a false statement.

A route parameter absorbs any URL segment, while a URL wildcard may only stand in for a literal route segment - that asymmetry keeps {model_id:path} routes matching without mislabelling ordinary parameter routes.
Helper URLs are resolved from call sites: consumeSSE(url, ...) has no URL of its own, and reading its name would have produced a wrong or empty row.
Routes without a browser caller are published as information, not as defects, because the CLI, the demo tour and the tests use the same API.

The story was re-done on a clean branch rather than merged from PR #104, so the runtime-program benchmark change it carried stays out of a UI/UX pull request; the generator and tests were ported rather than re-invented.

A dynamic match records its caller as possible on every candidate, never as certain on one: the literal argument at the call site is what proves which route runs, and a table that picks the first candidate invents that proof. The same rule makes 'no browser caller' a lower bound whenever any call site stays unresolved, which is why the map publishes caller_resolution.complete instead of leaving a reader to assume it.

evidence: The starting defect was not a lack of styling but a lack of vocabulary. Six surfaces reported a state and the redesign layer had flattened every .badge variant onto --text and --bg-hover, so .badge.green and .badge.red painted identically: the meaning survived only in the words, and the writers set the words and the colour on separate lines, which is how a chip ends up saying green FAILED after a one-line edit.

There is now one component - a label in --text, a dot and a hairline in one of six tones - and one writer, setStatus(tone, label), which takes both together so they cannot drift. Fifteen call sites moved onto it and no `className = "badge` writer remains in static/index.html.

The label is deliberately not painted with the tone. --text measures 12.98:1 on --bg-card in the dark theme and 15.79:1 in the light theme, while the dark --accent measures 3.30:1: fine for a dot that repeats the words, below the 4.5:1 a label needs. So the tone paints the dot and the hairline and the component stays legible in greyscale, where the words carry it.

The state table gained honest tones without changing a single label. failed, error and cancelled all shared amber with paused before; failure is danger now and cancellation is neutral. tests/test_task_events.py pinned the old colour classes and now pins the tones with the words unchanged, which is what makes the vocabulary change visible as a vocabulary change rather than a rendering change.

Evidence became a component rather than a convention: an .evidence block whose basis - measured, derived, unverified, unavailable - is a required attribute, a copy affordance that carries the basis with the claim, and one real application on Start, where the preflight summary states what was measured, at what time, and that no cloud provider was contacted. The four bases are the whole vocabulary; an unknown one throws.

Three pieces of proof, because declarations agreeing is not the same as a chip looking right. scripts/uiux_status_components.py fails the build on an undeclared or unused tone, a colour literal in a tone rule, a tone drawn for the hairline but not the dot, a converted surface that lost the component, no live region, a legacy badge writer, a state mapped to an unknown tone or to no words, an evidence basis outside the four, or a contrast regression. tests/test_status_components.py proves each check by breaking a temporary copy of the stylesheet, so the checks are exercised rather than trusted.

evidence: The defect was structural, not cosmetic: nine backdrops carried role=dialog, each open function added .open and each close function removed it, Escape removed it from all nine at once, no dialog trapped focus and exactly one of the nine remembered where focus came from. A keyboard user tabbed out of an open dialog into the page behind it and, on close, landed on the document body.

There is one controller now. openOverlay(id) records the return target, paints the backdrop, sets aria-modal, makes every element sibling of the backdrop inert and focuses the first control inside after the frame that paints it; closeOverlay(id) reverses all four in one place. Because the return lives there, Escape, a Close button and a backdrop click all return focus to the same control instead of three different outcomes.

The trap is belt and braces on purpose: inert is what actually stops Tab, clicks and screen-reader traversal reaching the background, and the Tab handler is the fallback for a browser without it, wrapping the cycle inside the dialog. The walk proves the fallback matters: two full cycles of Tab past the last control never left the dialog, on all nine.

Escape closes the top overlay only, not every overlay. The old one-liner lost the stack, so a dialog opened from another dialog vanished without returning focus to the one underneath - a behaviour no screenshot would show.

Focus return has a fallback for the case that made the old code give up: a chord pressed with the page focused has no opener, so the controller remembers the last control the user actually used (focusin) and returns there rather than to nothing. This is what makes Ctrl+K then Escape land on the palette's trigger.

The shortcut situation had the same shape as the statuses did in P1-03: the rail's Alt+N lived in data-shortcut, the palette's key lived in the handler, and the palette's hints were string literals beside neither, which is how Alt+6 stayed advertised and dead until P1-02. One registry now feeds the handler, the palette rows and the markup: every rail tab gained aria-keyshortcuts, and palette rows name their shortcut by id, resolved when the list is drawn.

Two palette rows were added because the story's acceptance criterion is keyboard reachability for every dialog: Start (which had no palette row at all) and the official Harness bridge. All nine dialogs now have a keyboard path, six through the palette and three through their own controls.

The inspector was a drawer with unstated behaviour. It declares aria-modal only while it covers the page (set on open, removed on close, never the invalid 'false'), takes focus when it opens below 1100px, returns focus to its toggle when Escape closes it, and drops the modal claim on resize when it becomes a column again.

Proof is measured, not asserted. scripts/uiux_overlay_inventory.py fails on a dialog that writes .open itself, a dialog without a label, a duplicate shortcut id or key, a palette item naming a shortcut that does not exist, a hard-coded Alt+N hint, an Escape handler that closes everything, and an inspector that never declares itself modal. tests/test_overlays.py proves each rule by breaking a temporary copy of the frontend, so a check that cannot fail would fail the suite.

decisions: inert is the trap, with the Tab handler as a fallback. A keydown-only trap leaks focus to the URL bar and to anything that receives focus programmatically; inert stops the background at the source, and the fallback keeps the promise on a browser without it.
Escape closes the top overlay rather than all of them. A stack is what makes nested dialogs coherent, and the old one-liner was a stack bug that looked like a feature.
aria-modal is set on open and removed on close, never set to "false". The attribute asserts that the dialog covers the page, and a closed drawer does not.

The return target falls back to the last control used, not to the document. Returning focus to <body> is the same as losing it; a chord pressed with nothing focused should still put the user back where they were.

Palette hints are resolved from the registry at render time instead of being written beside it. Two lists that can disagree is exactly how Alt+6 stayed advertised and dead; one list cannot disagree with itself.

The walk records a refusal as blocked, not as a pass. harnessDiffModal needs an active Harness session, the app says so, and this ledger says so - inventing a session to make the check green would prove nothing about the dialog.
